div.head: II Cn 35.1
div.ab: Witodlice, se ðe freondleasan ⁊ feorran cumenan wyrsan dom demeð þonne his geferan, he dereð him sylfum.
Witodlice, se ðe freondleasan ⁊ feorran cumenan wyrsan dom demeð þonne his geferan, he derað hym sylfum.
Scienter, qui amicis destituto uel extraneo deterius iudicium iudicat quam socio suo, se ipsum ledit.
Witodlice, se ðe freondleasan ⁊ feorran cumenan wyrsan dóm demeð ðonne his geferan, he derað him sylfum.
Witodlice, se ðefreondleasan and feorrancumenan wyrsan dom demeð þonne his geferan, he dereð him sylfum.
Wahrlich, wer einem Sippenlosen und fernher Gekommenen schlimmeres Urtheil zuerkennt als seinem Genossen, der schädigt sich selbst.
Truly, whoever gives a worse judgment to a man without kin and one come from afar than to his own fellow harms himself.
Verily, he who pronounces a more severe judgment upon one who is friendless or come from afar than upon one of his own acquaintances injures himself.
Assuredly, he who pronounces a worse judgment on a friendless man or a stranger from a distance than on his own fellows, injures himself.
Truly, whoever hands down a more severe sentence on the friendless or those come from afar than upon his own companions does injury to himself.
